speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you have had this painful ulcer on your leg, and have you noticed any changes in its size or appearance?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and uveitis, I need to rule out specific inflammatory conditions. Do you have any joint pain, abdominal cramping, or diarrhea that would suggest a flare of your Crohn's disease?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of a painful ulcer with a necrotic base and purplish borders at the site of a minor trauma, along with your history of uveitis, strongly suggests pyoderma gangrenosum rather than a simple infection or venous stasis ulcer. To confirm this diagnosis and rule out other causes, I need to examine the wound closely and check your inflammatory markers. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: ["Crohn's disease", 'Type 2 diabetes mellitus', 'Hypertension', 'Treated for anterior uveitis 8 months ago'] Social history: Recently returned from a visit to Wisconsin 2 months ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any fever, chills, or other systemic symptoms that might suggest an infectious cause for this ulcer?

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the classic presentation of pathergy following the ant bite and your history of inflammatory conditions, this is highly consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum. I will proceed with the final assessment based on these clinical findings. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma gangrenosum
